LESSON: WATER CONSERVATION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Conservation of Resources
Topic 1.2: Water Conservation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Water Conservation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we use drip irrigation to conserve water?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe drip irrigation as a way of conserving water

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WATER CONSERVATION
Subject: AGRICULTURE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Water Conservation helps you succeed in AGRICULTURE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT WATER
We use water for drinking, cooking, cleaning, and farming.
Conserve water: close taps, fix leaks, reuse grey water for plants where safe.
Unsafe water can cause disease — store drinking water in clean covered containers.

PART 1: Describe drip irrigation as a way of conserving water

What this means
In this part you learn to describe drip irrigation as a way of conserving water. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe drip irrigation as a way of conserving water.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Water Conservation” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe drip irrigation as a way of conserving water. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Water Conservation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Conserve water: close taps, fix leaks, reuse grey water for plants where safe.

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Water Conservation” around your school. (skill: describe drip irrigation as a way of conserving water)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Water Conservation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe drip irrigation as a way of conserving water.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Water Conservation from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Water Conservation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Water Conservation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we use drip irrigation to conserve water?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Water Conservation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe drip irrigation as a way of conserving water.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
